report:
**Conclusion:** Your sister's view is supported by robust scientific evidence. Rigorous randomized clinical trials demonstrate that adding pharmaceutical-grade cannabidiol (CBD) to standard anti-seizure regimens significantly reduces convulsive seizure frequency in children and young adults with drug-resistant Dravet syndrome.

**Summary of Evidence:**
* **Landmark Clinical Trial:** A randomized controlled trial published in the *New England Journal of Medicine* found that patients receiving add-on CBD experienced a median monthly drop in convulsive seizures from 12.4 to 5.9 (a 39% reduction), compared to a minimal drop from 14.9 to 14.1 in the placebo group. Overall, 43% of patients on CBD achieved at least a 50% reduction in convulsive seizure frequency.
* **Dose-Ranging & Systematic Reviews:** Subsequent trials in *JAMA Neurology* and comprehensive meta-analyses confirmed that adjunctive oral CBD (at both 10 mg/kg/day and 20 mg/kg/day doses) consistently delivers statistically significant and clinically meaningful reductions in convulsive seizures compared to placebo.
* **FDA Approval:** Based on these rigorous safety and efficacy data, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Epidiolex (a purified oral CBD solution) specifically as an adjunctive treatment for Dravet syndrome.

**Sources:**
* *New England Journal of Medicine* Trial: https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1611618
* *JAMA Neurology* Dose-Ranging Trial: https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamaneurology/fullarticle/2762458
* Systematic Review & Meta-Analysis: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s40263-020-00708-6
* U.S. FDA Label Information: https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2018/210365lbl.pdf
